text:
Kirill Kaprizov leads the league's goal race at 17 in 20 games and has points in nine straight, which is why his name keeps landing on lists next to the great left wingers. The chances are real: 12.9 expected goals is an elite number by itself, and Minnesota gets 59% of the expected goals at five on five with him on.

The finishing is the part that runs hot. He's shooting 27% after 17% last season, and the team has scored 4.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Our range for his shooting sits around 15 to 19%. The goals should slow; a 45-goal player having a 50-goal season is still the read.

He's also third of 515 skaters in wins added by goals this season, so the timing has been as good as the volume. The line with Matt Boldy and Joel Eriksson Ek is the story in Minnesota, and the rumor mill has started wondering aloud about pairing him with Nikita Kucherov. For now, watch whether the shot volume holds when the percentages cool.
headline: Kaprizov is scoring like a man in a hurry
